overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. Notices were timely posted for many subcommittee meetings, the Superintendent's advisory working groups fall under the Connelly exception, and minutes were created and posted for many meetings. Reminders issued only.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged no subcommittee posted notice for meetings held September 2019 to February 2020, though no specific meeting dates were identified.
allegations.key_passage: subcommittees of the Committee held numerous meetings between September 2019 and February 2020 for which notices were timely posted.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged advisory working groups (School Start Time, Wellness, DEI) were subcommittees that had to post notice and keep minutes; the Committee said they were Superintendent working groups.
allegations.key_passage: Because the working groups were created by an individual public official to advise her on decisions that she retained the sole authority to make, we find that they fall within the Connelly exception and are not public bodies subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged several subcommittees did not create, approve, or post meeting minutes in general, without identifying particular meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Nonetheless, based on information provided by the Committee and a review of the Harvard Public Schools’ website, we find that the subcommittees did create and post minutes for many meetings.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
